McLaren Circus Animals

By: Tarryn Crossman | Paid

Proposal


Show:

Further information:
THE CIRCUS



McLaren circus is the last circus in South Africa that still uses animals for entertainment, but not only do they have to perform night after night, but McLaren is also a traveling circus and these animals have been on the road since March 2021. They are shipped from city to city in a caravan of trailers and then let out into small pieces of land to stretch their legs between performances.



The circus has Tigers, Lions, camels, dogs, horses, alligators, pythons, and dogs, that according to owner David McLaren are all trained using positive reinforcement. McLaren claims that their animals are all born into captivity and therefore would never be able to live in the wild. Legally you can get a permit for performing animals as long as they are in ‘good condition’, they have water, food and shelter.



But the SPCA Wildlife unit says that they are trying to change this law to include animal welfare, which would include their mental well-being. This will hopefully be included in the first quarter of this year.

Effective as of Feb 2022 the law that stops all lion interaction is also supposed to have taken effect, which would make at least the Lions being used in the circus unlawful

When I spoke to SPCA WU director he didn’t seem to know if this was in fact coming into effect or how they would enforce this law.

He did mention that McLaren should have an import and then export permit to move the animals through each province, which as far as his office can see they don’t have. I am working on getting these details. These permits also outline the amount of space each specific animal should have and according to Smaragda , f ban animal trading, McLaren cages do not allow for even the minimum space required



Ban animal trading has been trying to amend the legislature on performing animal permits since 2015, but according to the director Smaragda Louw their pleas in parliament are falling on deaf ears.

Smaragda is a passionate animal rights activist who believes that even if an animal is born into captivity, they deserve a quality of life that goes beyond being forced to perform in a hot tent, under unnaturally bright lights, to a screaming crown, then put into a cage and shipped to the next town to perform again and again and again, until they are retired.



ACCESS

McLaren has said that they will allow us to come and film at the circus for a few days, including training sessions, backstage, the performance and then packing the animals up and moving them to the next location

David McLaren has agreed to be interviewed

Ban Animal trading will speak

SPCA WU director will speak

show with the dogs

DAVID
We've got specialised trailers that we've built to transport the animals comfortably

How many hours is that on average, that an animal would be in the space?
Animal can be granted for an hour to two hours.
Never more than two hours

This is roughly was roughly 15 by 10, and wherever you do go and you travel, is that roughly the same size

this is one of the reasons these circuses are getting banned everywhere in the world. The space that they have for those animals is completely inadequate.
At the ADI wildlife sanctuary, our smallest enclosures are a hectare. Our biggest are more like three four five.

I was very scared in the beginning

So when we see the trainer, Quintin, for instance, playing with the Lions and the Lion Princess of allowing him to put his arm in her mouth And it looked like a level of trust from both sides

you got the idea
